hypothesis: The F2-subspace structure of the factor base IS exploitable, by an oracle that is not a search at all, and the exploitation evaporates before it can matter. Concretely: Weil-descend S4(x1,x2,x3,x(R)) with each abscissa written in the V-basis, giving 131 Boolean equations in 3d unknowns. Prediction, stated before the confirming runs: (a) the system refutes a non-decomposable target at its own degree 6 with NO Macaulay multipliers -- i.e. some F2-linear functional lambda satisfies lambda(S4) = 1 identically, a linear NO-certificate computable in time polynomial in d; (b) that certificate exists exactly while the F2-affine span of the value set { S4(x1,x2,x3,x(R)) : xi in V } misses 0, which requires the span to be a proper subspace of F_2^131; and (c) the span saturates at 131 for small d, so the certificate dies far below the d = 45 at which decompositions begin to exist. If (c) holds the subspace route is a degenerate artefact in exactly the Kosters-Yeo shape RESEARCH_DREG_MEASUREMENT.md warns about, and the cheap regime and the useful regime do not overlap.
why_this_is_the_remaining_question: solver_12 and solver_13 closed the search-reorganisation routes: the Riemann-Roch encoding is Theta(|F|^2) with a constant worse than brute-force pair enumeration. The one place left for the falsification target of RESEARCH_ECC2K130_DECOMPOSITION.md section 5.3 to give is an oracle that exploits the algebraic structure of F rather than re-indexing a generic 3SUM search over it. Weil descent to F_2 in the subspace basis is the textbook way to do that (Gaudry, Diem, Petit-Quisquater), and it has never been run at n = 131: the repository's Rust implementation caps at n <= 64 because FieldStructure::new reduces structure constants through F2mElement::raw_bits().first(), a single u64.
curve: K_0 : y^2 + xy = x^3 + 1 over GF(2^131), ONB model, group order checked against the Koblitz recurrence as 4r with the published 129-bit prime. Same curve and same subspace factor base as solver_10, solver_12 and solver_13.
system: S4 in the elementary-symmetric form validated in solver_06 against src/cryptanalysis/koblitz_symmetrised.rs: e3^4 + (e4+1)*e3^2 + e4*(e4+1)*e1^2 + e1^4 on the four abscissas x1, x2, x3, x(R), with b = 1. Each xi = sum_j v_ij * b_j over the ONB basis of V, giving N = 3d Boolean unknowns; the 131 field coordinates give 131 Boolean equations.
measurements: M1 Algebraic normal form. For d = 2..5, build the exact ANF of all 131 equations by full Moebius transform of the truth table over all 2^(3d) assignments, and report the monomial count by degree. Expected multidegree (2,2,2) and total degree 6.

M2 Refutation degree. For the same d and a non-decomposable target, find the smallest Macaulay degree D at which F2 row reduction puts the constant 1 in the row space, counting the multipliers used. D = 6 with zero multipliers means the certificate is linear in the equations.

M3 Span boundary. For d = 4..12 and for d = 45 (the existence threshold) and beyond, sample assignments, accumulate the F2-affine span of the value set, and report its dimension and whether 0 is excluded. Several independent targets per d.

M4 Soundness gate. On PLANTED (decomposable) targets the value set contains 0, so no certificate may exist. Any planted target admitting a certificate is a correctness failure and invalidates the round.
falsification: The hypothesis is falsified if the span stays a proper subspace at d >= 45, since the certificate would then be available at parameters where decompositions exist -- which would be a genuine sub-quadratic decision oracle and a major result. It is also falsified if the refutation degree exceeds 6, or needs multipliers, at any measured d below saturation. The soundness gate M4 overrides everything: a certificate on a decomposable target means the construction is wrong.
limits: THE CERTIFICATE IS ONE-SIDED AND FINDS NOTHING. It can only prove that no decomposition exists; its absence proves nothing, and it never produces a witness. Section 3.2 of the background note converts a yes/no detector into a witness finder with k|F| further whole-base queries, but that conversion needs a detector that is correct in both directions, which this is not. M1 and M2 build the ANF by exhausting 2^(3d) assignments, which is a MEASUREMENT cost and larger than the brute-force search it is analysing; a deployed oracle would build the same ANF symbolically in poly(d), and no cost claim here rests on the exhaustive construction. M3's span dimension is computed from samples and is therefore a lower bound that rises to the true value; it is reported with the sample count and is stable well before the reported figure. Saturation at 131 is reported as measured on the sampled targets, not proved for all targets. No yield, Lambda, S or rho ratio is computed, and nothing here is an attack cost.
